newsitem.title: IRAN: Tajik government, opposition hold talks in Iran.
newsitem.headline: Tajik government, opposition hold talks in Iran.

text.p: Tajikistan's President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri met in Iran on Thursday for talks on achieving peace in the turbulent Central Asian country, state-run Tehran radio said.
The talks, held in the northeastern city of Mashhad, will cover an amnesty agreement, the disarming of opposition members and ways of guaranteeing their security, it said.

The two sides would also discuss the powers of a Commission of National Reconciliation to be formed under accords reached by senior officials of the Moscow-backed government and Islamist opposition leaders in two earlier rounds of talks since December, the radio added.
The issues are among outstanding differences after the accords which also included provisions on repatriating thousands of refugees and people displaced by four years of bloody conflict.

Opposition leaders have said the implementation of the accords has been hampered by a two-week crisis in which Tajik rebels seized hostages to pressure the government to allow a group of their men to join them from neighbouring Afghanistan.
The opposition has condemned the action of the rebel group.

On Tuesday, gunmen killed seven people in a spate of attacks in the Tajik capital Dushanbe, a day after the rebels released their hostages. Five of those shot were ethnic Russians. Moscow has thousands of peacekeeping troops in the volatile country.
A ceasefire, also part of the earlier accords, appears to be holding after the civil war that killed tens of thousands of people in the former Soviet republic of nearly six million.
